Salamanca borders Madrid, Cordoba borders Murcia and Madrid, and Toledo borders Teruel and Burgos, so I'm weighing whether to retake Burgos or shore up defenses at Vigo, Salamanca, and Toledo instead. My priority is pushing toward 18 conquered villages, currently sitting at 12 after Burgos flipped back to the enemy.

This turn my three armies in transit should resolve: Madrid likely falls given knight strength, while Teruel and Murcia attacks probably fail against stronger garrisons. Toledo's home forces are too weak to spare for offense, so I'll keep them defending against counterattacks from Burgos or Teruel, while the Badajoz army marching toward Madrid should secure that border village for me.

Burgos is still enemy-held and borders both Vigo and Toledo, but Vigo's available troops give an attack power of 13 against Burgos's defense of 15 -- not enough on their own. I'm considering whether sending multiple separate armies from different villages against Burgos could work sequentially, since attacks don't combine but might still stack as consecutive battles if the first one captures the village.

Given how weak our forces are relative to Burgos's defense, it's probably wiser to hold back this turn, consolidate, and focus on building up the economy rather than risking losses. I should instead reinforce Vigo with more knights before attacking, so the knight-counters-archer bonus actually kicks in.

Reinforcement takes time though, so maybe this turn is better spent consolidating and building troops for a bigger combined push later. Now I'm going through each village's wood/iron totals to plan builds: Lisboa gets a knight using all its wood and iron, while Santarem and Evora each pump out three spearmen using their full wood allotment, leaving their iron stockpiles idle for now. I'm considering whether Coimbra should build spearmen or shift some iron into an archer instead.

I'm now working through Vigo's larger wood and iron pool to figure out how many knights it can support.

For Vigo, I'm settling on one knight plus two spearmen since that uses up the wood almost entirely with iron to spare. Salamanca gets two spearmen for cleaner iron usage, Sevilha's numbers fit a knight and spearman exactly, Cordoba supports one knight with plenty of iron left, and Toledo mirrors the archer-plus-spearman pattern with some iron remaining.

Now I'm thinking about troop movements for defense—Toledo just fended off an attack and could face another wave, so I want to reinforce it. I'm considering an attack from Zaragoza to Madrid, where I could send a knight quickly. However, the enemy army is also arriving in Zaragoza soon, which complicates things since I only have one knight there. The defense at Madrid is weak, with only one archer. The knight counters the archer, so the attack should succeed.  

Then, I think about sending two knights from Murcia to Cordoba, but I've only got two knights available and the enemy gets reinforcements in a couple of turns. It might be a risky but strategic move to capture Cordoba for the village.**Prioritizing knight production**

I’m thinking about how each village can contribute resources and where to maximize my knight production. It seems I need to focus on building knights for the frontier. In Zaragoza, I could build one knight with 30 wood and 90 iron, but I wonder if I could stretch that to two? However, I only have 30 wood now, so that won’t work.  

In Murcia, I can build one knight with 30 wood and 40 iron, but I need to send existing knights. Plus, I see Pamplona can also build another knight.

I hold 17 of 24 villages, needing 18 to reach the 75% win threshold, then holding for two consecutive turns. Zaragoza and Pamplona are already counted among my 17, so I just need one more conquest. Tarragona looks like an easy target with only defense 8 and a small archer garrison.

Huesca is similarly weak and reachable from Zaragoza in one turn, while Castellon is much tougher. My army already marching toward Murcia (8 spearmen, 5 archers, 7 knights) faces a defending force that's also spearman-dominant, so neither side gets a counter bonus - and my calculated attack value of 46 comfortably beats their effective defense of 28.

Now I'm considering Zaragoza's remaining garrison (1 spearman, 4 archers, 2 knights, 17 attack power) to hit either Tarragona (def 8) or Huesca (def 5). Since both targets are weak, I'm weighing whether to split the force between them or send everything at one target to guarantee a decisive win rather than risk a narrow margin.

Actually Pamplona also borders Huesca and has a much stronger garrison (3 spearman, 7 knights, 31 attack power) - so it makes more sense to send Pamplona against Huesca for an easy, overwhelming win, freeing Zaragoza to focus its attack on Tarragona instead. I'm factoring in march speed, since mixing spearmen with knights slows the whole force to the spearman's pace.

Zaragoza's force (1 spear, 4 archer, 2 knight, 17 attack power) should comfortably beat Tarragona's defense of 8. Taking both villages would push me to 19 total, past my 18 target, though I'll need to hold them for two turns and shore up defenses at Zaragoza and Pamplona, which are now weak after recent losses.

Since counterattacks are a real risk, I should route reinforcements from interior villages like Toledo, Cordoba, and Teruel toward the border, and keep building knights given the ample resources. My plan: Pamplona sends 3 spearmen and 7 knights to Huesca for an easy win (31 vs 5 defense), Zaragoza sends its force to Tarragona, and Teruel holds its current defenses without splitting further since Cordoba's army is already en route to Murcia.

Now I'm working out build orders based on wood/iron costs for spearmen, archers, and knights, checking each village's current stock to figure out where knights can be afforded right now.

Since the win condition is nearly secured, I don't need to optimize every village -- I'll just add modest knight reinforcements to a few key border garrisons. Zaragoza and Toledo produce the most iron, but Zaragoza's home garrison is nearly emptied since most troops are marching out, so I need to account for that before deciding reinforcements there.

Emptying Zaragoza's garrison entirely leaves it defenseless if the enemy counterattacks, which would cost me a village toward the 18-village goal, so I should hold back some troops instead of committing everything. It might be safer to skip Tarragona this turn and redirect Pamplona's home troops against Huesca instead, keeping Zaragoza's defenders intact.

Since I already have 17 villages and just need one more to hit 18, I'll simplify by sending Zaragoza's full offensive force (1 spearman, 4 archers, 2 knights, attack 17) against Tarragona's defense of 8 for a clean win, while making sure Pamplona stays garrisoned.

Leaving Zaragoza empty is risky since attacks happen simultaneously this turn, but I'll accept it and use Zaragoza's remaining resources to build knights there instead - checking, Zaragoza has 30 wood and 80 iron, and a knight costs 30 wood and 30 iron, so I can still queue one up even without troops present.

At Pamplona, I have 30 wood and 20 iron, enough for one archer or two spearmen at 15 wood each - I'll go cheap with spearmen for quick defense. I also want to reinforce both cities from nearby villages like Burgos and Madrid that connect via roads, so I'll send Burgos's available knight over to Pamplona.

Madrid's army of one archer and one knight can reach Zaragoza directly since they share a road connection - I'll send that reinforcement too. Teruel borders hostile Castellón and Murcia so I'll keep its troops in place rather than diverting them, and Toledo doesn't have a direct route to either city so I'll skip it. I'm also weighing whether to use Teruel's forces to hit weak Huesca, which only has defense 5.

For Huesca, Pamplona holds 3 spearmen and 7 knights - I'll dispatch 5 knights plus 2 spearmen there since their combined attack of 22 easily overcomes Huesca's defense of 5, while leaving 1 spearman and 2 knights behind for some home defense.

Now I'm laying out the full set of orders: sending troops from Zaragoza to Tarragona, Pamplona to Huesca, and reinforcing Pamplona from Burgos and Zaragoza from Madrid, plus queuing builds - a knight in Zaragoza and two spearmen in Pamplona - while other interior villages keep churning out knights for later.

With resources piling up well below the cap, I figure it's worth adding modest builds elsewhere too - Lisboa can afford a knight using all its iron, while Santarem, Evora, Coimbra, and Porto lack enough iron for knights so I'm queuing archers instead, leaving small leftovers of wood and iron in each.

Continuing the pattern, Badajoz, Toledo, Cordoba, Teruel, and Madrid all have enough iron for a knight so I'm assigning those, while Faro, Salamanca, and Sevilha get archers plus spearmen where the leftover wood allows. This is getting complex, so I'm just going to keep working through each city methodically rather than trying to optimize perfectly.

I need to craft orders to survive incoming attacks in one turn. The enemy's attacks could come from unknown forces, so I have to exploit any captures I can manage. My current troop levels are small, and I'm focused on building local resources to afford maximum units quickly.

Huesca has 1 spear and 1 knight, but if the enemy has a majority of knights, it might tie, which isn't effective. If I go with a composition of 5 attackers (1 spear and 4 knights) against 6 defenders, I’d likely lose.

I could send 3 archers from Tarragona, but since the enemy is arriving in 1 turn, timing will matter. If I capture the empty spot, the enemy may attack afterward, making it tricky. I should send enough from both 12 and 13 to secure the area and consider the timing of reinforcements carefully.**Planning troop movements**

I’m thinking about sending 3 archers from 13 to 17, along with maybe 1 knight from Huesca to 17. However, that leaves Huesca with just 1 spear, making it vulnerable.

If I want to attack Madrid, I can’t bypass 17 since it’s currently empty. Cordoba from the Murcia route has an effective garrison of 8. I also have a big group at Murcia with 7 soldiers, 3 archers, and 1 knight, but I don’t want to abandon my position there. I’m considering sending those archers as well.

I've hit 20 villages, well above the 18/24 threshold needed—now I just need to hold that for two consecutive turns without dropping below. But an enemy army is closing in on Huesca, arriving next turn, and its defenses look thin with only a handful of troops available to send.

Castellon's garrison is strong so I won't touch it, and Tarragona/Murcia need to stay garrisoned as border villages. I don't know the incoming army's size, only its direction and timing, so I need to bolster Huesca immediately by pulling reinforcements from Zaragoza and Pamplona, both a turn away—though I need to check whether mixed troop speeds will slow the march down.

Since both routes support fast turns, I'll send Zaragoza's 2 knights and Pamplona's 3 knights to Huesca, bringing its total to 9 troops. I'm also checking if Zaragoza's archer can keep pace since its route allows a 1-turn medium march too, meaning I could send everything without delay.

Now I'm turning to Tarragona and Murcia, both recently captured border villages that could face counterattacks - Tarragona has just 4 troops and def 10, while Murcia has 13 troops and def 33, so I'm looking for interior villages to reinforce them. Teruel also borders the dangerous Castellon front with 10 troops on hand.

With most objectives already met, I'm deciding to prioritize defense over risky attacks, especially since Castellon's garrison looks too strong to challenge. I'll consolidate reinforcements at Huesca, Tarragona, Murcia, and Teruel, and use each border village's own wood and iron stockpiles to cheaply build extra spearmen or knights on top of the incoming reinforcements.

Wait, checking defense values - spearman, archer, and knight all have the same defense of 2, so unit type doesn't matter for defense purposes. That means I should just maximize troop count with the cheapest unit, which is spearman at 15 wood each with no iron cost.

Right, 2 spearmen at Huesca, leaving the leftover iron banked for next turn. Applying the same logic to Tarragona (2 spearmen from 30 wood) and Murcia (2 spearmen from 30 wood/50 iron), then moving on to check Teruel's 35 wood.

Continuing with Teruel (2 spearmen, 5 wood leftover), Zaragoza (2 spearmen using remaining iron after troop movement), and Pamplona (2 spearmen). Though these builds only become active next turn, not in time for this turn's incoming attack, they're worthwhile for future defense. The real question is whether reinforcements sent this turn to Huesca arrive before the enemy attack lands, since both seem to resolve on the same one-turn timing.

Given last turn's pattern of simultaneous resolution, I'll assume reinforcements merge with the garrison in time to help defend, so I'll proceed with sending them. For build orders, I'll place cheap spearman builds at villages with surplus wood, prioritizing border and capital growth while also adding modest builds at interior villages to keep expanding the army within resource limits.

I could expand builds to more interior villages for growth, but since the win condition is already met (20/24), I'll keep it modest and focus mainly on border defense and reinforcement rather than heavy expansion. Finalizing this plan now.

I'm thinking about how archers counter spears. If the enemy mostly has knights, that’s tricky because knights counter archers. If I have 5 troops attacking with a total of 8 offense, but the defense is 10, it looks like I'm likely to lose. I’ve sent them in already, but I wonder if there was a better strategy to employ here. Do I need to rethink my approach next time?

I need to shore up defenses - Zaragoza is dangerously thin with only 2 troops and def 5, while Huesca, Murcia, and Teruel are better garrisoned. The enemy from Tarragona could push toward Zaragoza next.

I should reinforce Zaragoza urgently from Toledo, Burgos, or Madrid, though those routes and travel times aren't fully clear from the road network given.

Considering options, pulling from Teruel or Huesca risks weakening those border villages which are already under threat, so I need to weigh which reinforcement source causes the least overall risk given the fog of war.

Since orders resolve simultaneously, any reinforcement I send this turn won't arrive in time to help against an attack happening right now -- Zaragoza's fate this turn depends solely on its current garrison, not what I dispatch.

Actually, even if Zaragoza falls, we'd drop to 18, which still meets the 75% threshold. Since last turn was already at 20 (above threshold), this turn at 18 would be the second consecutive qualifying turn, potentially triggering the win condition right away.

The risk is losing more than one village, since we only have 19 and can't drop below 18. So the priority is defending everything else while accepting Zaragoza (def5, 2 troops) as the likely loss. Teruel, Murcia, and Huesca all look reasonably fortified already, so I should still try to reinforce Zaragoza in case the attack goes elsewhere instead.

Since movement and combat both take a turn, reinforcements sent now might actually arrive in time to matter if enemy attacks also take a turn to land - meaning the garrison state at arrival, not right now, is what counts for the outcome.

Given that, sending troops from Huesca and Teruel to Zaragoza seems like a reasonable hedge. Huesca has 13 troops and only faces a weak threat from Girona (def5, 2 knights), so it can spare reinforcements safely while keeping enough to defend itself. Teruel also has a sizable garrison of 12 troops to draw from.

I'll send 3 knights from Huesca, leaving 5 spear, 1 archer, and 4 knights behind for defense, and pull some units from Teruel as well.

I could also route reinforcements from Toledo through Burgos and Madrid, slower but worthwhile for the longer term. Additionally, Zaragoza itself has enough wood and iron to produce more knights or archers locally, and I need to figure out whether freshly built units would count toward this turn's defense.

Actually, the rule seems to be that units built this turn become ready next turn, so they won't help defend right now. Given the win condition only needs holding 18/24 for two consecutive turns, I'll focus on solid defense and reinforcement rather than any risky attacks on the enemy capital.

My final plan: send knights from Huesca and Teruel to reinforce Zaragoza since they're fast, build up border villages using available resources, and consolidate interior troops at Toledo and Salamanca for future moves. I'm now writing the specific build order for Zaragoza with its troop and resource allocation.

For Zaragoza I'll settle on building one knight, using all 30 wood and 30 of the 90 iron for a solid attack/defense unit. For Huesca, with 35 wood and 90 iron, one archer plus one spearman fits perfectly at exactly 35 wood and 10 iron, leaving 80 iron in reserve. Now I'm turning to Teruel's 35 wood and 50 iron to work out a similar combination.

For Murcia's 30 wood and 70 iron, I'll go with two spearmen to use up the wood fully rather than an archer that would leave wood idle. For the remaining interior villages, since resources would otherwise sit unused, I'm leaning toward building modest troop numbers there too, given we're nowhere near the 300 cap and extra force projection can't hurt.

Actually, resources roll over turn to turn rather than being wasted, so there's no real urgency to spend them immediately without a concrete plan—since we're close to the win condition, defense may matter more than expansion. I'll focus construction on the border villages (Zaragoza, Huesca, Teruel, Murcia) and consider adding cheap spearmen at empty interior spots like Toledo, Burgos, and Madrid purely as a reinforcement pool. Checking Burgos specifically, its neighbors are all friendly territory, so it's safe for now, but with zero troops and zero defense it's still worth garrisoning with spearmen given its 90 wood and 80 iron.

Madrid similarly has no troops, so I'll build six spearmen there too using its wood. For reinforcements, I'm planning to pull knights from Huesca and Teruel toward Zaragoza—three from each—while leaving enough spearmen, archers, and knights behind in both to hold against their respective weaker enemy neighbors. I'll also route three knights from Toledo through Burgos/Madrid to Zaragoza as a slower backup, bringing the total incoming knights to nine, which combined with the existing garrison and new builds should give Zaragoza a solid defensive force.

I'll hold off on any move toward retaking Tarragona this turn since that risks overextending, and now I'm ready to finalize the plan and write it up.
